answer: Fingerprinted Clock Skew Attestation. Each agent identity must emit signed timing beacons whose drift is shaped by a device-bound cipher seeded at registration; the registry records that drift fingerprint and flags near-identical profiles. An attacker duplicating one identity must either clone the exact timing profile, which then collides visibly across nodes like a shared karst channel, or generate fresh seeds per copy, and each new seed costs a full hardware attestation plus a distinct opal-keyed calibration run, roughly hours of provisioning per duplicate.
